# Periodically validate the human experience against the intended experience

> **Headline:** Add a versioned, bot-baseline-derived **intended-experience
> targets** artifact plus a deterministic **human-experience validation**
> command that compares measured human (and bot) balance statistics against
> those bands, emitting a versioned JSON report and Markdown summary and
> failing with a non-zero exit code on drift.

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** feature · **Assignee:** Map

## Problem statement

Balancing is currently a manual, point-in-time activity. The automated-balancing
framework produces a stable, versioned `BalanceReport`, and the human-play
statistics work item produces the *same* statistics for real players — but
nothing states what the experience is *supposed* to be, and nothing periodically
checks the measured experience against it. This item turns the bot batch into
the **source of truth for intended experience** (recorded as explicit target
bands and mirrored into the GDD), then adds a repeatable validation that flags
drift in the measured human experience.

## Users

- **As a game designer / producer**, I want a periodic report comparing the
  measured human experience against explicit intended-experience targets, so I
  can see whether the game still plays as designed and where it has drifted.
- **As a game designer / maintainer**, I want the intended experience written
  down as machine-checkable targets derived from a bot baseline, so a tuning
  change can be judged against a recorded standard rather than remembered.
- **As a maintainer**, I want the same validation to run against a fresh bot
  batch, so a regression in the balance baseline is caught even before any human
  play is recorded.
- **As a producer**, I want a durable, versioned pass/fail artifact, so the
  experience of the game can be reviewed over time.

## Intended-experience definition (decision recorded)

The operator chose the **bot baseline** as the source of intended-experience
targets, with the **GDD updated to match**. Concretely:

- A bot batch (`npm run evaluate -- --batch`) produces the shared
  `BalanceAggregate`. Its per-metric distributions define the **target band**
  (centre = baseline mean/median; tolerance = a documented multiple of std-dev
  or a relative percentage).
- The resulting bands are committed as a **versioned targets artifact** — the
  single machine-checkable statement of intended experience.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` is updated so the *prose* intended experience
  (survival, pacing, progression, reward cadence) agrees with those bands.

This keeps one source of truth (the artifact) and one narrative (the GDD).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Versioned, machine-checkable targets.** A targets artifact (e.g.
   `src/data/experience-targets.json`) records, for each key metric of the
   shared `BalanceAggregate` schema — at minimum `survivalSeconds`,
   `mineralsCollected`, `upgradesSelected`, `waveReached`, `levelReached` and
   `avoidableHits` — a target band (centre + tolerance) plus a version
   constant, seeded from a recorded bot batch baseline. A test asserts the
   artifact validates against the schema and covers every required metric.
2. **Pure comparator.** A pure, clock-free, I/O-free module compares a
   `BalanceAggregate` (human **or** bot) against the targets and returns, per
   metric, the measured value, the target band, the signed drift magnitude and
   a pass/fail verdict. Unit tests cover in-band, above-band, below-band,
   missing-metric and empty-input cases, and assert no I/O / clock access.
3. **Periodic validation command.** A documented on-demand command (e.g.
   `npm run validate-experience -- <balance-report.json>`) reads a
   `BalanceReport`, compares it against the targets, writes a **versioned JSON
   report** and a **Markdown summary**, and **exits non-zero when any metric
   drifts beyond tolerance**. It labels the source (human / bot policy) in the
   output. Its scheduling (e.g. a documented cron/CI recipe) is documented but
   not built as CI infrastructure in this item.
4. **Determinism and reproducibility.** The same input report + targets yields
   byte-identical JSON and Markdown output; the pure core never reads the wall
   clock. Verified by tests (run twice, diff).
5. **GDD, documentation and test suite.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` is
   updated so the intended experience matches the bot-baseline-derived targets;
   the validation workflow, targets artifact and report shape are documented
   (extending `docs/BALANCING.md` and/or a new `docs/EXPERIENCE_VALIDATION.md`
   plus code comments/README as applicable); and the **full project test suite
   passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Blocked dependency:** this item depends on **Collect balance statistics
  from human player games (dev mode only)** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) — the human
  `BalanceReport` this validation consumes does not exist yet. Do not
  implement until that (and its helper child AH-0MV8ISO4O002HHDT) is
  delivered.
- Reuse the shared schema (`BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION`,
  `BalanceRunStats`, `BalanceAggregate`, `BalanceReport`) — no schema
  duplication.
- **Dev tooling only:** the targets artifact and validator are development
  tooling; no production game-code call site, no telemetry/consent change.
- Deterministic and byte-stable output; the pure core must not read the wall
  clock or perform I/O.
- No wall-clock/network dependency in the comparator; the `--batch` path is
  already reproducible and must stay so.

## Existing state

- **Shared schema:** `src/ai/eval/types.ts` defines `DistributionStats`,
  `BalanceRunStats`, `BalanceAggregate`, `BalanceReport`,
  `BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION` and `EVAL_DATASET_VERSION`
  (AH-0MV81YJQP008L9CQ, completed).
- **Bot batch:** `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` + `scripts/evaluate.mjs` write a
  byte-stable `balance-report.json` / `.txt` / `runs.jsonl` under `--out`
  (default `eval-output/`), documented in `docs/BALANCING.md`. A recorded
  100-game baseline exists in that document's acceptance-verification section.
- **Human stats (in progress):** **Collect balance statistics from human
  player games** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN, open) will emit a `BalanceReport`
  labelled with a `human` pseudo-policy. Its helper
  (`src/ai/eval/humanStats.ts`, AH-0MV8ISO4O002HHDT, blocked) does not exist
  yet.
- **No targets, comparator or validation command exists today.**
- **Related tuning loop:** **Automate the balance-tuning loop** (
  AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715, open) covers baseline/compare for *tuning*; this item
  covers *periodic experience validation* against a committed standard.

## Desired change

1. Add a versioned targets artifact (schema + initial bot-baseline values) and
   a loader/validator.
2. Add a pure comparator module producing per-metric drift + verdicts.
3. Add the validation CLI and a `package.json` script.
4. Add the JSON + Markdown report writers (byte-stable).
5. Add tests (schema, comparator, CLI, determinism) and update docs + GDD.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — add target/drift types + version constant (or a new
  `experienceTargets.ts`).
- `src/ai/eval/experienceTargets.ts` — pure targets loader + comparator
  (new).
- `src/data/experience-targets.json` — versioned intended-experience bands
  seeded from a bot baseline (new; exact path TBD at implementation).
- `src/ai/eval/experienceTargets.test.ts` — schema + comparator unit tests
  (new).
- `scripts/validate-experience.mjs` (+ `.d.mts`) — validation CLI (new).
- `scripts/validate-experience.test.ts` — CLI + determinism tests (new).
- `package.json` — add the validation script.
- `docs/EXPERIENCE_VALIDATION.md` and/or `docs/BALANCING.md` — document the
  workflow, targets and report shape.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — align the stated intended experience with
  the targets.

## Related work

- **Automated Balancing** (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) — epic that delivered the
  schema and batch runner.
- **Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only)**
  (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) — supplies the human statistics (dependency).
- **Shared human balance-statistics helper** (AH-0MV8ISO4O002HHDT) — the
  helper this item depends on indirectly.
- **Balance statistics schema and pure aggregation** (AH-0MV81YJQP008L9CQ) —
  the shared schema.
- **Automate the balance-tuning loop: baseline, single-edit, re-run and diff**
  (AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715) — related baseline/compare tooling.
- Docs: `docs/BALANCING.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md`,
  `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/TELEMETRY.md`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the bot batch is a *directional* proxy for the human
  experience (documented fidelity boundary in `docs/BALANCING.md`). Target
  bands are therefore intentionally tolerant; an out-of-band *human* result is
  a prompt to investigate, not proof of a bug.
- **Risk (dependency):** implementation is blocked until the human-stats item
  lands; the brief can be finalised now but must not proceed to implementation.
- **Risk (target inflation):** deriving targets from the bot baseline makes the
  bot trivially self-consistent; the comparator's value is against *human*
  stats. Document this explicitly so a green bot run is not mistaken for proof
  of a good human experience.
- **Risk (tolerance tuning):** too-tight bands cause false drift alarms; too
  loose hide real regressions. Mitigation: state the tolerance rule in the
  artifact and document how to adjust it.
- **Scope-creep risk:** CI scheduling, dashboards and automatic ticket creation
  on drift are *out of scope*; scheduling is documented only.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Where should the initial *intended-experience targets* come from?**
  — Answer (operator, interactive): **Bot baseline, and update the GDD to
  match.** The bot batch's aggregate distributions define the target bands; the
  GDD is edited so its prose intended experience agrees. Source: interactive
  reply.
- **Q: What form should the "periodic" run take?**
  — Answer (operator): **As recommended** — an on-demand, deterministic
  validation command with documented scheduling (no CI cron infra is added in
  this item; the repo has none today). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q: What should the validation emit?**
  — Answer (operator): **Versioned JSON + Markdown summary + exit code**
  (non-zero on drift). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q: What is the current state of the shared schema and human stats?**
  — Answer (agent, research): The shared schema is delivered
  (`src/ai/eval/types.ts`, AH-0MV81YJQP008L9CQ); the human-stats collection is
  still open (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) and its helper
  (`src/ai/eval/humanStats.ts`, AH-0MV8ISO4O002HHDT) does not exist. This item
  is consequently `blocked` for implementation. Research: `wl show` +
  `ls src/ai/eval/`. Source: repository.
- **Q: Does a targets artifact or validator already exist?**
  — Answer (agent, research): No. Research: `ls src/ai/eval/`, `grep` of
  `docs/BALANCING.md`. Source: repository.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW** – Automated Balancing (completed)
- **AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN** – Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only) (open)
- **AH-0MV8ISO4O002HHDT** – Shared human balance-statistics helper (blocked)
